rows.raw:
SN1 ka rate sirf substrate concentration par depend karta hai:

\[
\text{Rate} = k[\text{R–X}]
\]

Slow step = leaving group ka departure aur carbocation formation. Nucleophile concentration rate ko affect nahi karti.

rows.raw:
The rate of an **SN1 reaction** is controlled by the concentration of the **substrate only**:

\[
\text{Rate} = k[\text{substrate}]
\]

The slow, rate-determining step is **C–leaving group bond ionisation** to form a carbocation. The nucleophile attacks afterward, so its concentration does not affect the SN1 rate.

A substrate that forms a more stable carbocation generally undergoes SN1 faster:

\[
3^\circ > 2^\circ \gg 1^\circ
\]

Benzylic and allylic substrates can also react quickly because resonance stabilises the carbocation.
